atoms.b: As the Anglo-Saxons became more organised and powerful, new threats to their ((++kingdoms bikes)) began to emerge.
((++Vikings Australians)) started raiding the British coast and even started to take settlements.
The Anglo-Saxons now had to develop a new strategy to fend off these ((++raids trading_parties)).

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: To defend against Viking attacks, King Alfred developed a new plan for defence. He reformed the tax system to be able to build new fortified settlements called burhs.

Alfred wanted many burhs to be built so that all villages would have one within 20 miles. No matter where a Viking army attacked, a burh would always be close enough to raise an army for defence. They were also built at important points, such as river crossings, so that any attacking army would have a hard time ignoring them.

These towns soon became centres of trade and ((++culture crime)), and some of them still exist today!
